text: Do not use any of these standard containers: `std::vector`, `std::deque`, `std::list`, `std::forward_list`, `std::array`, `std::basic_string`, `std::string`, `std::stack`, `std::queue`, `std::valarray`.

Store the numbers in memory you allocate yourself (`new[]`, or `malloc`/`realloc`) and grow the block when it is full, so that memory use follows the actual input size. A fixed-size array, or a single allocation sized for the largest possible input, does not satisfy this constraint.

Release every block you allocate: when the array grows, the old block is freed (or `realloc` is used), and the last block is freed before the program ends (a destructor that frees it counts). A program that allocates nothing passes this constraint.
